title: Feature-first feature catalog
description: A whole-file array of feature records. Each record preserves user intent and links it to validation, proof, routines, and how-to documentation.

id.description: Stable feature identifier. Do not recycle an ID when a feature is renamed or deprecated.

status.description: Current delivery state, independent of lifecycle maturity. Use partial when only some behavior or supporting research exists.

lifecycle.description: Product lifecycle state. Verified requires observable proof; accepted means the intent is recorded, not that delivery is complete.

story.description: Cockburn User-Goal altitude, phrased as an 'I can…' user outcome. Keep implementation nouns out of the story; implementation belongs in linked routines or notes.

jobStory.description: Optional Jobs-to-be-Done framing: 'When [situation], I want [motivation], so I can [outcome]'. Null means the situation/motivation framing is not yet known.

algorithm.description: Optional ordered user-specified/inferred behavior model, used where one feature describes a multi-step workflow. It is not a technical plan.

validation.description: Executable-style acceptance scenarios plus explicit evidence that would invalidate the feature claim.

scenarios.description: Gherkin-inspired Given/When/Then scenarios describing observable user outcomes, not implementation steps.

invalidation.description: Concrete counter-evidence that shows the capability is absent, broken, or incomplete. Avoid vague checks such as 'does not work'.

criteria.description: Feature-level observable proof criteria. These resemble review-dash ProofCriteria but are not engine-native records.

linkage.description: Must explain that the review-dash engine is keyed by Notion task-page ID; feature criteria must be referenced by a criteria-file path or task ID and cannot be embedded as a feature-ID-native engine payload.

engineRef.description: Optional bridge to engine-native proof. Keep null until a real task page and criteria file exist.

taskId.description: Notion task page ID consumed by the engine, if assigned.

criteriaPath.description: Path to engine-native criteria JSON, if generated.

routine.description: Pointer to an inventory-grade ordered routine contract, or an explicit null reference with a reason. A routine describes trigger, inputs, and ordered actions; it is not an implementation plan.

id.description: Stable routine ID, such as RT-F-01, or null when no routine is defined.

ref.description: Path/anchor to the routine contract, or null.

reason.description: Why the routine reference is null, or what the linked routine covers.

trigger.description: Manual, scheduled, or event trigger; null when not established.

inputs.description: User-visible inputs consumed by the routine.

steps.description: Ordered, inventory-grade actions. Empty when no routine contract exists.

skillDoc.description: Pointer to the how-to-use documentation for the capability, including planned documentation when it has not been written.

ref.description: Documentation path/anchor, or null if no location has been chosen.

status.description: Whether the how-to documentation exists, is planned, or has no known home.

reason.description: Context for a planned or absent document, or what the present document teaches.

provenance.description: Required provenance preserving the user's exact words and source message. Never paraphrase quote; use spec-derived only where the inventory explicitly says the wording is synthesized from a specification.

messageId.description: Source message identifier as recorded in the feature inventory.

quote.description: Verbatim source quote. When the inventory supplies multiple fragments, retain each fragment exactly and separate them without rewriting.

confidence.description: Whether this is a direct quote, a user correction, or a spec-derived formulation. Spec-derived records should carry the provenance caveat in notes.

ambiguities.description: Open questions not settled by the user. Keep uncertainty visible rather than silently selecting a behavior.

notes.description: Scope, implementation-state evidence, decisions, or provenance caveats that do not belong in the user story.

links.description: Stable cross-catalog links for feature → extracted user story → routine → proof items → how-to document.

storyId.description: Stable ID used when projecting this feature into app-skills-extraction user-stories.json.

routineId.description: Stable routine catalog ID, or null until a routine is defined.

proofIds.description: Stable IDs of the feature-level criteria items.

skillDocRef.description: Same canonical how-to documentation pointer as skillDoc.ref.

id.description: Stable scenario identifier scoped to the feature.

proofCriterion.description: A stable, feature-level proof item shaped like (but not embedded as) review-dash screenshot criteria.

id.description: Stable proof identifier, such as PC-F-01-01.

slug.description: Compact stable slug corresponding to engine ScreenshotCriteria.slug when adapted.

description.description: What observable result this proof checks.

expected_values.description: Named expected observations compatible in spirit with the engine's expected_values map.

evidence.description: Expected evidence artifact or observable source; use a concrete path, screenshot, event, or user-visible state where known.

status.description: Current proof state. Do not mark pass without evidence.

action.description: Verb describing the user-facing or agent-facing action.

target.description: The session, agent, result, or other object acted on.

description.description: What the step accomplishes and what completion looks like.

order.description: One-based order in the user-facing behavior model.

text.description: Concise behavior statement; keep unresolved implementation mechanics out of specified behavior.

basis.description: Whether the behavior was explicitly specified by the user or is an inference requiring confirmation.

provenance.description: Verbatim source evidence for a specified algorithm step.

quote.description: Verbatim source text supporting this step.
